## Overview

Linear-combination splits allow each internal node to split on a weighted combination of several variables rather than a single predictor. This can help when the signal is carried by a direction such as `X1 + X2` instead of one coordinate at a time.

The example below uses regression. The same idea can also be applied to classification and survival forests by setting `model = "classification"` or `model = "survival"` and choosing a model-appropriate `linear.comb.method`.

## Regression Example

```{r regression-data}
set.seed(3)

n <- 160
p <- 6
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
colnames(X) <- paste0("X", seq_len(p))

y <- 1 + X[, 1] + X[, 2] + 0.5 * X[, 3] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)

train_id <- 1:120
trainX <- X[train_id, ]
trainY <- y[train_id]
testX <- X[-train_id, ]
testY <- y[-train_id]
```

Fit a regression forest that considers linear combinations of up to three variables at a split. Here `linear.comb.method = "sir"` selects sliced inverse regression (SIR), which uses the response to estimate a predictor direction. The tree then searches for a cutpoint along that direction. With `nsplit = 3`, it compares three random candidate cutpoints; `nsplit = 0` would search all available cutpoints.

```{r linear-combination-fit}
library(RLT)

fit_lc <- RLT(
  trainX, trainY,
  model = "regression",
  ntrees = 200,
  nmin = 5,
  mtry = 3,
  nsplit = 3,
  linear.comb = 3,
  linear.comb.method = "sir",
  ncores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

print(fit_lc)
```

Linear combinations do not require `reinforcement = TRUE`; this fit uses the default `reinforcement = FALSE`.

## Prediction

```{r linear-combination-predict}
pred <- predict(fit_lc, testX, ncores = 1)
test_pred <- pred$Prediction

list(
  Test_MSE = round(mean((test_pred - testY)^2), 4),
  Maximum_Combination_Size = fit_lc$parameters$linear.comb
)
```

The held-out mean squared error summarizes prediction error on the 40 observations excluded from fitting. It describes this simulated dataset and fit. The stored combination setting confirms the maximum of three variables, not the number used at every split.

## Other Model Types

For classification, use `model = "classification"` with methods such as `"lda"`, `"naive"`, `"random"`, or `"logistic"`.

For survival, use `model = "survival"` with methods such as `"coxph"` or `"naive"`.
